newsitem.title: FRANCE: Borotra urges increased French car ind cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Borotra urges increased French car ind cooperation.

text.p: French Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Monday that one way for French carmakers to prepare for competition in the year 2000 could be through increased industrial cooperation.
"The effect of economies of scale will be a determining effect," Borotra told a news conference.
He confirmed that the government was studying ways to help the car industry adapt to increased competition in 2000 when the European Union removes remaining protective quotas on imports.
"The battle will be over price," he said. It was important to help carmakers preserve their position and to increase their competitiveness so that they can cut their prices.
Borotra said it was important to preserve two French carmakers into the 21st century, not just in Europe but globally.
He declined to give further details of the government strategy. "It's too early to discuss that yet," he said.

He said the industry ministry could not ignore an industry that directly and indirectly employed 700,000 people, represented 17 percent of French industrial production and generated 450 to 500 billion francs of turnover.
